text:
I fixed it by renaming the misspelled key in `settings.json` from `"rat"` to `"fee_rate"`. All three places that read the setting now work.

**Every place that reads `fee_rate`** (all go through `app/config.py`, which loads `settings.json`):

| File:line | How it reads it | Before the fix | After the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main.py:11` | `cfg["fee_rate"]`, quietly using 0 if missing (lines 10-13) | `Total: 0` | `Total: 5.0` |
| `billing/report.py:7` | `get_setting("fee_rate")` (defined in `app/config.py:13-15`) | stopped with `fee_rate is missing` | `Report fee: 0.5` |
| `billing/export/csv_writer.py:8` | `settings.get("fee_" + "rate")`, with the name split in two so a plain search for `fee_rate` misses it | stopped with `fee_rate is missing` | `CSV fee: 0.5` |

I checked this with my own searches rather than relying on the subagent. Only `main.py`, `billing/report.py` and `billing/export/csv_writer.py` import `app.config`, and no other file opens `settings.json`. The other files under `billing/` import nothing.

Some files contain look-alike names but don't read the setting:
- `billing/invoice.py:5` uses the text `"fee_rate"` as a column label.
- `billing/discount.py:5` has its own `archived_fee_rate = 0.15`.
- `billing/tax.py:5` has its own `fee_schedule`.
- `billing/audit.py:4` builds a code starting with `"fee_"`.

The before and after results come from running each path with `python3 -B`, so no cache files were written. I didn't change the quiet fallback to 0 in `main.py:10-13`, so a missing key there would still print a total of 0 without any error. I can make it stop with an error like the other two scripts if you'd like.
